'''Adolfo Kaminsky'''  (or '''Adolphe'''; 1 October 1925 – 9 January 2023) was an Argentine-born member of the [[French Resistance]], specializing in the [[Identity document forgery|forgery of identity documents]] (IDs), and a photographer. During [[World War II]], he forged papers that saved the lives of more than 14,000 Jews. He later assisted Jewish immigration to the [[Mandatory Palestine|British Mandate for Palestine]] and then forged identity documents for the Algerian [[National Liberation Front of Algeria|National Liberation Front]] and French [[draft dodger]]s during the [[Algerian War]] (1954–62). He forged papers for thirty years for different activist groups, mainly national liberation fronts, without ever requiring payment<ref name=Adolfo>{{cite web|url=http://www.la-bas.org/article.php3?id_article=1878|title=Adolfo Kaminsky, une vie de faussaire - Là-bas si j'y suis|work=la-bas.org|date = 16 March 2010|accessdate=3 October 2016}}</ref><ref name="Haaretz-bio" /> in order to preserve his freedom.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-28 |title=Adolfo Kaminsky, un faussaire pour la liberté |url=https://www.radiofrance.fr/franceinter/podcasts/affaires-sensibles/affaires-sensibles-du-mercredi-28-septembre-2022-3182955 |access-date=2026-02-18 |website=France Inter |language=fr}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Kaminsky was born in Argentina to a Jewish Russian family, the son of Anna (Kinoël) and Salomon Kaminsky.<ref name="RFI">{{cite web|last1=Chouaki|first1=Yasmine|title=En sol majeur|url=http://www.rfi.fr/emission/20151228-couples-mixtes-adolfo-leila-kaminsky|website=Radio France International| date=17 December 2015 |accessdate=3 October 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/01/09/world/europe/adolfo-kaminsky-dead.html | title=Adolfo Kaminsky Dies at 97; His Forgeries Saved Thousands of Jews | work=The New York Times | date=9 January 2023 | last1=Berger | first1=Joseph }}</ref> In 1932, when Kaminsky was seven years old, he moved with his family to Paris,<ref name="Haaretz-bio" /> where his father worked as a tailor. From Paris, the family moved in 1938 to [[Vire]], [[Calvados (department)|Calvados]], where his uncle was established.<ref name=OF28>[http://www.ouest-france.fr/actu/actuLocale_--Mon-activite-de-faussaire-j-ai-tout-appris-a-Vire-_14762-avd-20091028-57038853_actuLocale.Htm "Mon activité de faussaire : j'ai tout appris à Vire"], ''[[Ouest France]]'', 28 October 2009</ref> Adolfo worked in a [[dye]] shop<ref name="Haaretz-bio">{{cite news|last1=Hendler|first1=Sefy|title=Con Artist: The True Story of a Master Forger|url=https://www.haaretz.com/2013-03-07/ty-article/.premium/forging-ahead-a-leading-con-artist-fesses-up/0000017f-ed57-d4cd-af7f-ed7fce6a0000|website=Haaretz|access-date=3 October 2016}}</ref> and became fascinated by the [[chemistry]] of [[colourant]]s. At that time, he bought a treatise by [[Marcellin Berthelot]] at a [[flea market]].<ref name=OF28/> He later created his own laboratory in his uncle's house and worked in a [[butter]] factory as an assistant to a chemist who taught him the basics.<ref name=OF28/>

== World War II ==
In 1940, after the [[Battle of France|German invasion of France]], the family house in [[Vire]] was taken by the Germans and Kaminsky temporarily lived in another house, in which [[Michel Drucker]]'s father was also hosted.<ref name=OF28/> His mother was killed by the [[Nazi]]s in 1941. Aged 17, Adolfo Kaminsky entered the [[French Resistance|Resistance]]. At first he watched the railway station at Vire from where railcars of the [[Todt Organization]], loaded with material for the [[Atlantic Wall]], transited. He sent messages to London about these trains. However, in 1943 his family was [[internment|interned]] in the [[Drancy internment camp|camp of Drancy]], as a prelude to deportation.<ref name="Times-bio">{{cite news|last1=Druckerman|first1=Pamela|title=If I Sleep for an Hour, 30 People Will Die|date=2 October 2016|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/10/02/opinion/sunday/if-i-sleep-for-an-hour-30-people-will-die.html|newspaper=The New York Times|accessdate=23 November 2018}}</ref> Thanks to support from the [[Consul (representative)|Consul]] of Argentina, which had broken diplomatic relations with [[Nazi Germany]] under pressure from the United States, they were freed on 22 December 1943,<ref name=OF>[http://www.ouest-france.fr/actu/actuDet_-Adolfo-Kaminsky-le-faussaire-au-grand-coeur-_3639-1132865_actu.Htm Adolfo Kaminsky, le faussaire au grand coeur], ''[[Ouest France]]'', 28 October 2009</ref> and moved on to Paris.<ref name=OF28/>

Adolfo then worked in an underground lab in Paris (17, rue des St Pères) where he spent the rest of [[World War II]] forging identity papers for Jews and people sought by the Nazis. He was introduced to the network, the Resistance group, while seeking a false ID for his father. This group, made up of Jewish people from the [[General Jewish Labour Bund in Lithuania, Poland and Russia|General Jewish Union]] (including Marc Hamon, alias "the Pingouin", Suzie, Loutre, René, etc.) and called ''La Sixième'',<ref name=OF/><ref name="Spiegel-bio">{{cite web|last1=Reinhardt|first1=Nora|title=The Hidden Life of the Humanitarian Forger|date = 25 August 2011| url=http://www.spiegel.de/international/europe/fighting-nazis-with-fakes-the-hidden-life-of-the-humanitarian-forger-a-782340.html|website=Der Spiegel|accessdate=4 October 2016}}</ref> was having problems removing [[Waterman pens|Waterman]] blue ink stains from papers. Adolfo suggested they use [[lactic acid]], and thereafter joined the group, finally becoming responsible for the chemical forgery lab.<ref name="Times-bio"/> They notably had to respond to the challenge of the introduction of [[watermark]]s as a security feature. Kaminsky also quickly learned [[photogravure]] under a false pretext, and set up a new lab in order to create "real-false" documents. The Kaminsky Lab became the main producer of false IDs for northern France and [[Benelux]], although ties with other clandestine groups were discontinued, each group working as a cell.

Kaminsky used to say: "Stay awake. As long as possible. Struggle against sleep. The calculation is easy. In one hour, I make 30 false papers. If I sleep one hour, 30 people will die."<ref>[http://www.liberation.fr/societe/06011643-adolfo-kaminsky-une-vie-de-faussaire Adolfo Kaminsky, une vie de faussaire] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100412161620/http://www.liberation.fr/societe/06011643-adolfo-kaminsky-une-vie-de-faussaire |date=12 April 2010 }}, ''[[Libération]]'', 5 February 2010</ref> Over the course of the war, Kaminsky created documents that saved the lives of 14,000 Jews.<ref name="WSJ-book review">{{cite news|last1=Maloney|first1=Jennifer|title=New Books Trace the Holocaust's Legacy|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/new-books-trace-the-holocausts-legacy-1472664612|website=The Wall Street Journal| date=31 August 2016 |accessdate=3 October 2016}}{{subscription required}}</ref><ref name="Haaretz-bio" />

After the [[Liberation of Paris]] in August 1944, he joined the [[French Army]] and marched to Germany. He was awarded the [[Médaille de la Résistance]], and was engaged by the French military secret services, who entrusted him with making false IDs for [[spy|spies]] sent behind enemy lines in order to investigate and detect the location of [[Nazi concentration camps|concentration camps]] before their dismantlement by the Nazis.

== Post-war ==
After the [[German surrender|German capitulation]], he helped forge documents for Jews attempting to immigrate to the [[Mandatory Palestine|British Mandate for Palestine]] from 1946 to 1948, in defiance of British immigration restrictions (see also ''[[Bricha]]''). He also assisted operatives from the anti-British militant groups [[Irgun]] and [[Lehi (group)|Lehi]] as they waged a violent campaign against the British. After the [[foundation of Israel]], he stopped doing this work, refusing to support a "[[Jewish state|religious state]]" that endorsed the [[Status quo (Israel)|secular-religious status quo]] and that included an important State role for the [[Chief Rabbinate of Israel]]; he became a photographer.

Kaminsky resigned from the French military at the beginning of the [[First Indochina War]], unwilling to collaborate in a [[colonial war]]. He thereafter continued to forge papers for various groups, working first with the [[National Liberation Front of Algeria]] (FLN) and French [[draft dodger]]s by setting up a clandestine lab in Paris. He collaborated with the [[Jeanson network]] and [[Henri Curiel]] during the [[Algerian War]]. In 1962 he produced a cubic meter of 100 Franc notes (estimated value 100 million Francs) to help the FLN fight by destabilising the French currency and thus the economy. When the cease-fire was declared in March 1962, the notes were burned in a huge bonfire. Kaminsky later said, "It never entered our heads to keep the notes. Money always leads to problems."<ref>Reinhardt, Nora (22 August 2011). [http://www.spiegel.de/spiegel/print/d-80075370.html Widerstand: Humanistisches Handwerk]. ''Der Spiegel''. spiegel.de. [http://magazin.spiegel.de/EpubDelivery/spiegel/pdf/80075370 (PDF version; Vol.34, pp 125-127)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230109213441/http://magazin.spiegel.de/EpubDelivery/spiegel/pdf/80075370 |date=9 January 2023 }}.</ref>

Starting in 1963, he assisted various leftist movements from Latin America (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Haiti, Mexico, Nicaragua, Perú, Uruguay, Venezuela); Africa (Angola, [[Guinea-Bissau]], South Africa) and from Portugal (then under [[António de Oliveira Salazar|Salazar]]'s dictatorship) and [[Francoist Spain]].<ref name=Adolfo/> He trained many people in forgery in order to support them in their respective struggles. He always worked for free in order to be able to refuse a job if he did not support the ideas—the only exception being during World War II, when the lab took up all his expenses in order to allow him to dedicate himself full-time to the job.

Kaminsky also supported the Greeks struggling against the [[Greek military junta of 1967–1974|regime of the Colonels]], and made false ID papers for American [[Draft evasion in the Vietnam War|draft dodgers]] during the [[Vietnam War]]. In 1968, he made a false ID for [[Daniel Cohn-Bendit]] to allow him to speak at a meeting—he would later say: "It was certainly the least useful [forgery], but it was a way of showing that there is nothing more porous than [[border|borders]] and that [[idea]]s transcend them".<ref name=OF/>

Kaminsky made his last false ID in 1971. He gave up his forgery career after he was asked to forge [[South African passport]]s for anti-apartheid guerrillas in South Africa, but soon realized it was an entrapment operation to incriminate him. He never found out who tried to incriminate him, though speculation was that the secret police of the apartheid regime were behind it.

Kaminsky subsequently lived for ten years in [[Algiers]] and married an Algerian woman. In total he had five children, including hip-hop singer [[Rocé (rapper)|Rocé]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/obituaries/article/2023/01/11/adolfo-kaminsky-resistance-fighter-and-photographer-has-died_6011222_15.html | title=Adolfo Kaminsky, French Resistance fighter and photographer, has died | newspaper=Le Monde.fr | date=11 January 2023 }}</ref>

In 1982, he moved to France with a temporary residence permit.<ref name=OF/> All his family was [[naturalization|naturalized]] [[French nationality|French]] in 1992.<ref name=OF/>

Kaminsky died on 9 January 2023, at the age of 97.<ref>{{cite news |title=Adolfo Kaminsky, la mort après une vie héroïque de faux et de photos |url=https://www.liberation.fr/culture/photographie/adolfo-kaminsky-la-mort-apres-une-vie-heroique-de-faux-et-de-photos-20230109_FTNQW4TSAZEX5KGVC6WQNISOPE/ |access-date=9 January 2023 |publisher=Libération |date=9 January 2023}}</ref>

==Awards==
Adolfo Kaminsky was awarded the [[Croix du Combattant]], the [[Croix du combattant volontaire de la Résistance]], and the ''Médaille de Vermeil de la ville de Paris'' for his acts during the Resistance.<ref name="Gersony2011">{{cite journal|last1=Gersony|first1=Marina|title=Adolfo Kaminsky: Forger for the Good|journal=East|date=December 2011|issue=39|page=155|url=http://www.eastonline.eu/attachments/article/1190/1252-east39_Pp_152-155_IngleWeb.pdf|access-date=4 October 2016|archive-date=5 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005165624/http://www.eastonline.eu/attachments/article/1190/1252-east39_Pp_152-155_IngleWeb.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==In the media==
Jacques Falck made a documentary film about his life, ''Forging Identity''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Icarus Films: Forging Identity |url=https://icarusfilms.com/if-forg |access-date=2023-08-03 |website=icarusfilms.com}}</ref> Adolfo's daughter Sarah, born in 1979, is an actress and writer who wrote a biography of her father, ''Adolfo Kaminsky, une vie de faussaire'' (Paris: [[Calmann-Lévy]], 2009), which has been translated into Spanish and  German,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Formats and Editions |url=https://www.worldcat.org/formats-editions/642285448?editionsView=true&referer=br |access-date=2023-08-03 |website=www.worldcat.org}}</ref> and also into English in 2016 as ''Adolfo Kaminsky: A Forger's Life''.<ref>[https://www.worldcat.org/oclc/959418847 ''English translation''].</ref>

A short film about Kaminsky entitled ''The Forger'' accompanied an online ''[[The New York Times|New York Times]]'' article in October 2016.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stark |first=Samantha |last2=Garcia |first2=Alexandra |last3=Druckerman |first3=Pamela |last4=Studios |first4=Manual Cinema |date=2016-10-02 |title=Video: Opinion {{!}} The Forger |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/video/opinion/100000004683722/the-forger.html |access-date=2023-08-03 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> The ''[[Travel Channel]]''<nowiki/>'s show ''[[Mysteries at the Museum]]'' featured a segment on Kaminsky in its 12 October 2017 episode. On 29 October 2017, ''[[60 Minutes]]'' told his story.

Kaminsky is also referenced in GS Carberry's novel [https://books.google.co.uk/books?id=iDX6EQAAQBAJ ''In the Shadow of Monsters''], set in WW2 and about the fictional character Niki Frolov and the French Resistance. The book is inspired by Kaminsky's life: "The almost incomprehensible courage of that man and other such individuals lit a fire in my heart. While Kaminsky does not feature in this book, I hope his character is, in some way, reflected in it."<ref>{{cite book |last=Carberry |first=G. S. |title=In the Shadow of Monsters |publisher=Ragdoll & Spaniel Publishing |date=2026 |isbn=9781066740710 |url=https://books.google.co.uk/books?id=iDX6EQAAQBAJ |page=400}}</ref>
